 New Federal Data Reveals the Worst US Airline for Holiday Travel
 Travel Host Follow Al Chumba, Dana Sullivan Kilroy Sat, October 24, 2026 at 2:07 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Sat, October 24, 2026 at 2:07 PM UTC A cheaper airfare can become an expensive mistake if a delayed flight causes a missed connection, a lost hotel night or a missed cruise departure.
 With Thanksgiving and Christmas approaching, recent airline performance data offers travelers another factor to consider before booking beyond the ticket price.
 A new analysis of federal aviation data compares eight major U.S. carriers using their August arrival records and cancellation rates.
 Advertisement Advertisement The findings reveal a substantial difference between early-morning departures and evening flights, giving travelers another way to weigh their options.
 Delta Leads August DOT Data With 77% On-Time Arrival Rate
 Delta Air Lines recorded the highest on-time arrival rate among the eight carriers in the analysis, while JetBlue Airways finished last.
 The figures come from an analysis by Global Work & Travel of the U.S. Department of Transportation's October 2026 Air Travel Consumer Report, released October 19 covering August operations.
 For this comparison, an arrival counts as on time if the aircraft reaches its destination within 15 minutes of schedule.
 The ranking was:
 Advertisement Advertisement Delta Air Lines: 77.0% on-time arrivals
 Allegiant Air: 73.2%
 Alaska Airlines: 72.3%
 United Airlines: 71.7%
 American Airlines: 70.6%
 Southwest Airlines: 69.1%
 Frontier Airlines: 64.4%
 JetBlue Airways: 59.7%
 The results do not guarantee how an airline will perform during the holiday rush. August figures reflect one month of operations, and weather, airport congestion and other disruptions can change performance from season to season.
 The Transportation Department's report provides the underlying official data.
 Bloomberg / Getty Images
 JetBlue Cancels 6.2% of Flights as Allegiant Drops to 0.4%
 Arrival punctuality was not the only difference between the carriers.
 Cancellation rates varied considerably, with Allegiant recording the lowest rate and JetBlue the highest in the same comparison.
 Advertisement Advertisement Allegiant canceled 0.4% of its flights in August, followed by Southwest at 0.8%. JetBlue canceled 6.2%, while Frontier had the second-highest rate at 3.0%. Delta's cancellation rate was 2.0%.
 Those differences can matter when a trip depends on reaching a destination on a specific day. A canceled flight can require rebooking and potentially disrupt connecting transport, accommodation or a cruise departure.
 "Look at the route, the departure time, the connection and the other flights available that day," said Jurgen Himmelmann, co-founder and CEO of Global Work & Travel, in comments reported by TravelPulse .
 6 a.m. Departures Hit 89.7% Punctuality vs. 52.8% at 8 p.m.
 The analysis also examined scheduled departure times across the 30 largest U.S. airports.
 Advertisement Advertisement Flights scheduled between 6 and 6:59 a.m. were on time 89.7% of the time, compared with 52.8% for departures scheduled between 8 and 8:59 p.m.
 That is a notable difference, although it only reflects the period studied. Earlier departures may also require an expensive taxi or an overnight hotel stay if public transportation is not running.
 For holiday trips where arrival time matters, travelers should compare an airline's recent performance with the specific route, available backup flights and connection times. If a missed arrival would derail an important commitment, traveling a day earlier may provide more protection than choosing a lower fare.
